tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

tools.name: spawn_teammate
tools.description: Create one named, durable teammate. Only the Team Lead may call this tool.

description.description: Short description of the delegated responsibility.

prompt.description: Complete initial task for the teammate.

context.description: fresh starts without Lead history; fork inherits completed Lead turns. Defaults to fresh.

tools.name: subagent
tools.description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool starts an independently managed subagent and immediately returns its id. The runtime notifies you when it finishes. The child reports results with `send_message`; use `send_message` to steer it while running or continue its conversation after it finishes.

cwd.description: Initial child working directory. Relative paths use your current directory; omitted inherits it. Later directory changes in either agent are independent.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The complete, self-contained task for the subagent. It does not share this conversation's context, so include everything it needs.

tools.name: subagent_fork
tools.description: Delegate a task to a subagent that inherits this conversation: a child agent seeded with all completed turns so far (it does not see the current in-flight turn). Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool starts an independently managed subagent and immediately returns its id. The runtime notifies you when it finishes. The child reports results with `send_message`; use `send_message` to steer it while running or continue its conversation after it finishes.

cwd.description: Initial child working directory. Relative paths use your current directory; omitted inherits it. Later directory changes in either agent are independent.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The task for the subagent. It already sees this conversation's completed turns, so build on them freely and state only what is new.

tools.description: Create one unowned pending task on the shared Team task board.

description.description: Complete task details and acceptance criteria.

blocked_by.description: Task ids that must complete first.

write_scopes.description: Advisory workspace-relative file or directory prefixes this task expects to modify.

expected_revision.description: Current task revision used as the CAS precondition.

action.description: Task transition to apply.

description.description: Replacement details for edit.

blocked_by.description: Complete blocker list for set_dependencies.

write_scopes.description: Replacement advisory write scopes for edit.

owner.description: Member target from spawn_teammate or list_agents for Lead-only reassign; omit to unassign.

tools.description: Record and update a task list to plan multi-step work and show progress; skip it for trivial single-step tasks. Add one todo per concrete step before you start. todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

tools.description: Update the current goal.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

tools.description: Read the current working directory, or change it with cd. Relative paths use the current directory. Existing shells and running processes keep their own directories.

cd.description: Existing directory to enter. Omit to read the current directory.

tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend. Provide `file_path` before `content` in the arguments.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

   Also **team decision panel** and **hero detail** maybe fixed width; inspect.

1: class_name NetKillFeed extends Control
2: ## P3e 击杀战报带：监听 host 经 NetSession 广播的 show_kill_feed 全部战报（击杀/终结/名刀/塔/龙/出兵）。
3: ## 复刻主机 UI_Manager._create_kill_feed_panel：顶部中央（自顶向下 y=100×ui_scale 起）、黑底 0.6 半透明衬底、
4: ## 三段式（actor / desc / victim）字号 16×ui_scale，配色与主机一致：actor 敌橙/其余青，
5: ## victim 己青/敌橙/中立紫；1.0s 停留 + 0.5s 淡出。
6: 
7: const SHOW := 1.0
8: const FADE := 0.5
9: const GAP := 4.0              # 同 host HBoxContainer 默认 separation
10: const BASE_Y := 100.0         # 同 host panel.position = Vector2(-100, 100) * ui_scale
11: const FONT_SZ := 16.0         # 同 host _apply_label_style(..., 16, ...)
12: const ENEMY_C := Color(1.0, 0.33, 0.264)
13: const CYAN_C := Color(0.0, 0.886, 1.0)
14: const PURPLE_C := Color(0.75, 0.5, 1.0)
15: 
16: var _items: Array = []   # [{actor:String, a_team:int, desc:String, victim:String, v_team:int, born:int(msec)}]
17: var _f := UiKit.font()
18: 
19: # 同主机 UI_Manager.ui_scale()
20: func _us() -> float:
21: 	return UiKit.scale()
22: 
23: func _ready() -> void:
24: 	mouse_filter = Control.MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE
25: 	set_anchors_and_offsets_preset(Control.PRESET_FULL_RECT)
26: 	NetSession.net_kill_feed.connect(_on_kill_feed)
27: 
28: func _on_kill_feed(actor: String, actor_team: int, desc: String, victim: String, victim_team: int) -> void:
29: 	# host 开局链经战报通道转发的纯音频（SFX:: 前缀）：剥掉本地播、不画横幅
30: 	if desc.begins_with(SfxManager.ANN_PREFIX):
31: 		SfxManager.play_announce(desc.trim_prefix(SfxManager.ANN_PREFIX))
32: 		return
33: 	SfxManager.play_feed(actor, actor_team, desc, victim, victim_team)
34: 	_items.push_back({"actor": actor, "a_team": actor_team, "desc": desc,
35: 			"victim": victim, "v_team": victim_team, "born": Time.get_ticks_msec()})
36: 	if _items.size() > 5:
37: 		_items.remove_at(0)
38: 	queue_redraw()
39: 
40: func _seg_w(txt: String, sz: float) -> float:
41: 	return _f.get_string_size(txt, HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_LEFT, -1, sz).x
42: 
43: func _draw() -> void:
44: 	var vp := get_viewport()
45: 	if vp == null:
46: 		return
47: 	var area := vp.get_visible_rect().size
48: 	var us := _us()
49: 	var fs := FONT_SZ * us
50: 	var gap := GAP * us
51: 	var line_h := fs * 1.55
52: 	var now := Time.get_ticks_msec()
53: 	var rows: Array = []
54: 	for it in _items:
55: 		var age := (now - int(it["born"])) * 0.001
56: 		if age < SHOW + FADE:
57: 			rows.append(it)
58: 	_items = rows
59: 	if rows.is_empty():
60: 		return
61: 	# 单行文本总宽（actor [desc] victim 三段式），逐行自顶向下铺开
62: 	for ri in range(rows.size()):
63: 		var it: Dictionary = rows[ri]
64: 		var a: String = str(it["actor"])
65: 		var d: String = str(it["desc"])
66: 		var v: String = str(it["victim"])
67: 		var a_team: int = int(it["a_team"])
68: 		var v_team: int = int(it["v_team"])
69: 		var ac := ENEMY_C if a_team == Config.Team.ENEMY else CYAN_C
70: 		var dc := Color(1, 1, 1)
71: 		var vc := CYAN_C if v_team == Config.Team.PLAYER else (ENEMY_C if v_team == Config.Team.ENEMY else PURPLE_C)
72: 		var segs: Array = []
73: 		if a != "":
74: 			segs.append([a, ac])
75: 		segs.append([d, dc])
76: 		if v != "":
77: 			segs.append([v, vc])
78: 		var total := 0.0
79: 		for s in segs:
80: 			total += _seg_w(str(s[0]), fs)
81: 		total += gap * (segs.size() - 1)
82: 		var x := (area.x - total) * 0.5
83: 		var y := BASE_Y * us + ri * line_h
84: 		var age := (now - int(it["born"])) * 0.001

395: 		return Vector4.ZERO

397: 	var sx := vs.x / float(win.x)
398: 	var sy := vs.y / float(win.y)
399: 	return Vector4(

1144: func _anchor_br(ctrl: Control, from_br: Vector2, size: Vector2, inset: Vector2 = TOUCH_CLUSTER_INSET):
    from_br += inset
    ctrl.anchor_left = 1.0
    ctrl.anchor_top = 1.0
    ctrl.anchor_right = 1.0
    ctrl.anchor_bottom = 1.0
    ctrl.offset_left = -from_br.x - size.x
    ctrl.offset_top = -from_br.y - size.y
    ctrl.offset_right = -from_br.x
    ctrl.offset_bottom = -from_br.y
    
    func _anchor_tl(ctrl: Control, from_tl: Vector2, size: Vector2):
    ctrl.anchor_left = 0.0
    ctrl.anchor_top = 0.0
    ctrl.anchor_right = 0.0
    ctrl.anchor_bottom = 0.0
    ctrl.offset_left = from_tl.x
    ctrl.offset_top = from_tl.y

@'
extends Node
func _ready() -> void:
	var ui = preload("res://scripts/ui/UI_Manager.gd").new()
	add_child(ui)
	await get_tree().process_frame
	await get_tree().process_frame
	print("UI_PROBE_VP=", get_viewport().get_visible_rect().size, " win=", get_window().size, " scale=", ui.ui_scale())
	for nm in ["recall_indicator", "team_decision_panel"]:
		var c = ui.get(nm)
		if c: print("UI_PROBE_", nm, " rect=", c.get_global_rect())
	var hero = preload("res://scripts/entities/Hero.gd").new()
	hero.yuanliu_picked = false
	ui.show_yuanliu_pick(hero)
	await get_tree().process_frame
	for c in ui.get_children():
		if c is Panel and c.size.x > 500.0 and c.size.y > 500.0:
			print("UI_PROBE_yuanliu rect=", c.get_global_rect())
	hero.free()
	get_tree().quit()

已修复手机端 UI 越界问题，主要原因是中心面板使用了错误的定位方式。

**修复内容**
- **回城指示器、团队决策面板、元流之子流派选择面板**：之前中心锚点下直接写 `position`，被当成父级绝对坐标，导致面板跑到屏幕外（流派选择面板甚至大半在左上角外）。已改为用 `offset` 居中。
- **触控层安全区**：摇杆、普攻/技能/召唤师/回城/主动装等右下角按钮整体避让刘海、圆角、底部手势条；桌面端安全区为 0，布局不变。
- **小地图、目标信息框、属性面板、头像带**：补充左侧/顶部安全区内缩，避免被挖孔遮挡。
- **商店抽屉**：宽度不再固定 2280，窄屏会按视口收窄，避免左右溢出。
- **联机触控层**：手机端隐藏桌面 WASD 移动模式切换键，避免窄屏从左侧越界。

**验证**
- 宿主 `battle.tscn`、客户端 `net_client.tscn` headless 编译无 SCRIPT/PARSE 错误。
- 按 2340×1080（虚拟画布 3033×1400）模拟检查：回城指示器、团队决策面板、流派选择面板均完整落在屏幕内；其中流派面板矩形约 `x=1056..1977, y=154..1246`。

## 召唤师技能名 → 图标类型（不在表内的一律通用圆环）
## 在圆形按钮里画图标：深色底盘 + 元素色光环 + 白色/同色线稿图形；dim=不可用（压暗）
static func draw_icon(ci: CanvasItem, center: Vector2, radius: float, kind: String, dim := false) -> void:
ci.draw_circle(center, radius, Color(0.05, 0.06, 0.09, 0.90 if not dim else 0.94))
ci.draw_circle(center, radius * 0.92 * t, Color(col.r, col.g, col.b, 0.035))
ci.draw_arc(center, radius - 1.0, 0, TAU, 40, Color(col.r, col.g, col.b, 0.75 if not dim else 0.35),
static func _motif(ci: CanvasItem, c: Vector2, k: float, kind: String, col: Color) -> void:
"tower":  # 推塔：三层防御塔 + 底部波纹

ci.draw_rect(Rect2(c.x - 0.60 * k, c.y - 0.08 * k, 0.84 * k, 0.62 * k), col)
ci.draw_line(c + Vector2(0.44 * k, 0.70 * k), c + Vector2(0.44 * k, -0.10 * k), col, w, true)
"recall":  # 回城：传送门 + 下坠箭头（蓝）

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "Get-Process" → "List running processes".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap; on expiry the command moves to the background as a job instead of being killed.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

summary.text:
## Primary Request and Intent
- Earlier: generate new minion models fitting the map; show screenshots first, apply after confirmation.
- Follow-up: `"可以，你还有主宰先锋的模型没有生成"` — minion direction approved, dragon vanguard still needed.
- Then: `"接入吧，确保这些模型都有移动、攻击和死亡动画"` — integrate all seven models with movement, attack, death animations.
- Then: `"请把对局界面UI的布局再调紧凑一点；目前AI的寻路指引感觉看起来和地图质感不是很搭，请你调整"` — compact battle HUD and restyle AI path guide.
- Then: `"请你优化游戏性能（主要针对新加的特效，让游戏不要太卡顿）"` — optimize performance, mainly newly added VFX. This work was completed and delivered.
- Current: `"手机端界面似乎有点问题，有些地方超出屏幕了"` — mobile UI overflow; identify and fix off-screen UI.

## Key Technical Concepts
- Godot 4.7.2, GDScript, Forward Mobile renderer; no tests/CI; main scene `scenes/battle.tscn`.
- Engine binary: `D:\Downloads\06_游戏与Flash资源\Godot_v4.7.2-stable_win64.exe\Godot_v4.7.2-stable_win64_console.exe`.
- Headless compile: `--headless --path . scenes/battle.tscn --quit-after 45`; same for `scenes/net_client.tscn`.
- `project.godot`: `window/size/viewport_width=2400`, `viewport_height=1400`, `stretch/mode="canvas_items"`, `stretch/aspect="expand"`, `handheld/orientation=4` (sensor landscape).
- Virtual canvas: height fixed 1400, width = device aspect × 1400, generally ≥2400 for 16:9/20:9 phones, but ~1866 for 4:3 tablets and ~2240 for 16:10.
- UI scale: `UiKit.scale()` = `maxf(1.0, viewport_width / 2400.0) * 1.35`; fonts multiply by this, most fixed offsets do not.
- Safe area helpers in `UiKit`: `safe_insets()`, `safe_top()`, `safe_bottom()`, `safe_left()`, `safe_right()`, `apply_safe_top()`, `apply_safe_bottom()`; only mobile returns non-zero.
- Critical Godot semantics verified by a SceneTree probe: after `set_anchors_and_offsets_preset(Control.PRESET_CENTER)`, setting `position = Vector2(-w/2, -h/2)` places the control at absolute parent coordinates (negative/off-screen), NOT relative to center. Must use `offset_left/top/right/bottom` to center.
- Host touch controls in `scripts/mobile/TouchController.gd`; net-client touch controls in `scripts/net/NetTouchPad.gd`; both use bottom-right `_anchor_br()` geometry copied from the same literals.
- `MoveModeToggle` is desktop-only in host (`visible = ... and not OS.has_feature("mobile")`), but `NetTouchPad` created it unconditionally and anchored it 1600px from right, which overflows virtual widths <1930.
- Net client HUD is a separate `Hud` class; top score strip uses old 520×188 geometry at `cx-160..cx+360`, not the compact host HUD.
- Windows notification required before delivery: `pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts\dev\notify.ps1 -Title "HonorKing · ..." -Message "..."`.

  `pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts\dev\notify.ps1 -Title "HonorKing · <任务名>" -Message "<一句话结果>"`
  （脚本已就绪，失败会静默降级，不阻断交付）。

## Project Overview

HonorKing — a 3D MOBA game built with **Godot 4.5** (Forward Plus renderer). All game logic is written in **GDScript**. The game simulates a 5v5 Honor of Kings-style match: one player-controlled hero plus 4 AI teammates versus 5 AI enemies across a three-lane map with jungle, turrets, and epic monsters.

## Development Commands

- **Run the game**: Open `project.godot` in the Godot 4.5 editor and press F5, or run `godot --path .` from the project root.
- **No tests, no build step**: There is no test suite or CI. The only way to verify changes is to run the game in the Godot editor.

## Architecture

### Autoloads (Globals)

Defined in `project.godot` → `[autoload]`. These singletons are available everywhere without `load()`:

| Autoload | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `Config` | `scripts/core/Config.gd` | Constants: `MAP_SIZE=120`, `Team` enum (`PLAYER=0, ENEMY=1, NEUTRAL=2`) |
| `ItemDatabase` | `assets/ItemDatabase.gd` | All item definitions, synthesis trees, recommended build paths, `get_item()`, `can_build()`, `get_synthesis_cost()` |
| `SkillDatabase` | `assets/SkillDataBase.gd` | All skill definitions (hero skills + summoner spells), `get_skill()` |
| `GameManager` | `scripts/core/GameManager.gd` | Stub — currently empty (`_ready` and `_process` are no-ops) |
| `UiManager` | `scripts/ui/UI_Manager.gd` | Comprehensive UI: skill icons, shop, kill feed, hero detail panel (C key), target info, death recap, buff panel, damage/gold/heal popups |
| `CollisionSystem` | `scripts/core/CollisionSystem.gd` | Per-frame entity pushback to prevent overlapping (heroes ← → turrets, minions ← → turrets excluded) |

### Core Scripts (`scripts/core/`)

- **`BattleManager.gd`** — The central game controller (`class_name BattleManager`). Handles:
  - Map creation (ground planes, lane planes, river, high-ground circles)
  - Hero select UI → game start flow
  - Player hero + AI hero creation (one of each role: assassin/mage/marksman/warrior/support)
  - Turret, jungle camp, wall/bush placement
  - Minion wave spawning (3 lanes × 2 teams, with growth tables, siege/super/dragon minion variants)
  - Epic monster timers (Tyrant at 4min, Dragon at 4min)
  - Economy systems: kill/assist gold, tower gold, lane gold sharing, natural gold/exp, jungle item rules, support item rules
  - Input handling: left-click attack order, right-click move, raycasting for ground/target selection
  - Camera: follows player hero, minimap drag/jump override
  - Win condition: crystal destruction → game-over screen
  - Hero configs: `hero_configs` dictionary with base stats for all 17 heroes

- **`EntityDatabase.gd`** — Stub (empty `_ready`/`_process`).

- **`CameraController.gd`** — Standalone camera script (attached to a Camera3D), follows a `@export var target`. Currently unused — BattleManager controls the camera directly.

- **`MapGenerator.gd`** — Alternative map generator (creates a simpler 60×60 grass + river). Not used in the main game; BattleManager has its own `_create_map()`.

- **`CollisionSystem.gd`** — See Autoloads above.

### Entity Hierarchy (`scripts/entities/`)

All entities inherit from **`GameEntity`** (`class_name GameEntity extends CharacterBody3D`):

```
GameEntity
├── Hero (player & AI champions)
├── Turret (defensive structures)
├── Minion (lane creeps)
├── JungleMonster (neutral camps + epic monsters)
├── Bullet (projectile for ranged attacks and skill shots)
├── LinearBullet (directional projectile variant)
├── Wall (terrain obstacle)
├── Bush (stealth zone)
├── HealthPack (regen pickup)
├── TeleportZone (teleport pad)
└── prw (unidentified entity)
```

**`GameEntity`** provides:
- Base stats: `health`, `max_health`, `attack`, `armor`, `magic_resist`, `move_speed`, `attack_range`, `attack_speed`, `body_radius`, `level`
- State effects: slow, stun, knockup, freeze, suppress, silence, grievous wounds
- Shield system (`shield_remaining`/`shield_timer`)
- Marker system for stacking passives (e.g., Zhen Ji freeze, Angela burn, Marco Polo stacks)
- Damage calculation: `take_damage()` with armor/MR reduction formula (`resistance / (resistance + 602)`), penetration, crit detection
- Hunt DoT system (jungle item burn)
- Lifesteal application (physical and magical, with grievous wounds reduction)
- Death handling: `die(killer)` → signals, gold/exp distribution, buff transfer
- Kill assist detection (nearest enemy hero within 12 units)

**`Hero`** (`scripts/entities/Hero.gd`, ~2150 lines) — The largest and most complex class:
- **Stats**: base stats + role-based growth per level (tank/warrior/assassin/marksman/mage/support)
- **Equipment**: 6-slot inventory, `buy_equipment()` with component synthesis, `_apply_equipment_bonuses()` recalculates all stats from items, 100+ unique item passive/active effects
- **Skills**: 3 hero skills + summoner spell + recover, each with cooldowns, mana costs, charge/restore system, upgrade via Ctrl+key or auto-level
- **Hero-specific logic**: Each hero has hardcoded special behavior in `_physics_process()` (Arthur passive heal + W shield rotation, Donghuang orbs, Li Bai sword auras, Zhang Fei transformation + mana, Lanling stealth, Taiyi Q channeling)
- **Combat**: auto-attack with bullet spawning (ranged) or instant (melee), crit, on-hit effects from 20+ items
- **Input**: WASD movement, right-click move orders, left-click attack orders, skill hotkeys 1-3, summoner spell key, item actives (keys 6-0, V, =, -)
- **Post-game stats**: `damage_dealt_to_heroes`, `damage_taken_from_heroes`, `healing_done`, `cc_duration_dealt`, `turret_damage`, `jungle_gold`, `last_hits`, `gold_history`

**Other entity notes**:
- `Bullet.gd` / `LinearBullet.gd` — Projectiles with speed, damage, pierce, slow, red buff burn, team affiliation
- `Turret.gd` — Auto-attacks nearby enemies, has outer/inner/high/crystal tiers with different stats
- `Minion.gd` — Follows waypoints along lanes, attacks enemies in range
- `JungleMonster.gd` — Has `activity_radius` (leash range), `buff_type` for red/blue buff
- `Wall.gd` / `Bush.gd` — Static collision/stealth volumes
- `HeroAI.gd` — AI controller for bot heroes (attached as child of Hero)

### Asset Scripts (`assets/`)

- **`ItemDatabase.gd`** — Massive dictionary of all equipment items with: name, tier (1-4), cost, stat bonuses, `requires` (synthesis components), `passive`/`active` descriptions, category tags. Key functions: `get_item(id)`, `can_build(id, owned)`, `get_synthesis_cost()`, `get_synthesis_tree()`, `get_recommended_items(role)`.
- **`SkillDataBase.gd`** — Dictionary of all skills (hero abilities + summoner spells). Each skill defines: `type` (0=targeted, 1=AoE, 3=linear, 4=dash, 6=shield), `cooldown`, `mana_cost`, `cast_range`, `damage`, `radius`, `duration`, etc.
- **`Skill.gd`** — Skill resource class (`class_name Skill extends Resource`). Properties: `skill_name`, `type`, `cooldown`, `cd_bonus`, `mana_cost`, `power_bonus`, `cast_range`, `cast_time`, `damage`, `radius`, `duration`, `self_displacement`, `shield_amount`, `is_channeling`, `charge`, `restore`, `restore_bonus`.

### UI System (`scripts/ui/`)

**`UI_Manager.gd`** (~1600 lines) handles all in-game UI:
- Skill bar with 8 icon slots (4 skills + summoner + 2 active equipment)
- Shop system (O key): categorized grid (物理/法术/防御/靴子/打野/游走/保命), detail panel, buy/sell, component synthesis display
- Recommended equipment (B key to quick-buy)
- Kill feed (multi-kill announcements, tower/epic monster kills)
- Hero detail panel (C key): team stats, all hero cards with stats/skills/equipment/KDA
- Death recap (auto-shows on death): damage source breakdown with stacked bar charts
- Target detail panel (shows selected target's stats)
- Buff/debuff display panel
- Damage/heal/gold floating numbers (world-space → screen projection)
- Respawn widgets (hero icons with HP rings and respawn timers)

Internal classes: `SkillIcon` (draws cooldown overlay, upgrade indicator), `RespawnWidget` (HP ring + death timer), `DamageChart`.

### Key Mechanics to Understand

1. **Damage formula**: `actual_damage = raw_damage × (1 - resistance / (resistance + 602))` where resistance already accounts for flat and percentage penetration.
2. **Attack speed**: Uses a threshold table (Model A from Honor of Kings) — panel AS% maps to discrete attack interval tiers.
3. **Economy sharing**: Multiple heroes near a minion kill split gold (100%/80%/55%/43%/37% for 1-5 players). Jungle/support items modify this.
4. **Minion growth**: Minion stats interpolate from growth tables at `game_time / 60` minutes, with melee/ranged/siege/super/dragon variants.
5. **Item synthesis**: Buying a high-tier item that requires owned components only costs the difference. Selling refunds 70%.
6. **Buff system**: Active buffs are stored as dictionaries with timers, processed each frame in `_calculate_buff()`. Red/blue buffs transfer on kill.
7. **Hero-specific code**: Each hero has unique mechanics hardcoded with `if display_name == "..."` checks in `_physics_process()`, `_perform_attack()`, and `_finish_casting()`. Adding a new hero requires touching Hero.gd in multiple places plus adding skill definitions to SkillDatabase.

### Assets Not Tracked in Scripts

- `icon.svg` — Game icon
- `.godot/` — Engine cache (shader cache, editor state, import files)
- `scenes/battle.tscn` — The single main scene (binary .tscn format)
- 3D models, textures, and audio are created programmatically (PlaneMesh, CapsuleMesh, TorusMesh, StandardMaterial3D) — there are no imported art assets.

Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

We could extend wall payload style; but maybe user only cares host visuals. Yet net client should match. Need think of minimal robust solution.

Goal "提高地图外周墙壁的质地，使它们看起来无缝结合" — likely visual only. We can:
- Add a **new continuous perimeter wall mesh** generated by `MapVisuals` or `BattleManager` in host (not tied to Wall nodes), rendered as a single/4 long segments with seamless stone courses; hide outer per-wall visuals.
- For net clients, add same continuous mesh via a new method `MapVisuals.build_outer_wall(parent)` and call on both host and net client. Since map perimeter is fixed coordinates (same map), no network payload needed. This is elegant: both host and client build the perimeter rampart from fixed geometry. Keep existing `Wall` collision nodes for physics; just make their visuals hidden for perimeter. For net clients, `NetModels.wall` still displays per-wall visuals unless we skip perimeter walls in client and build continuous. We can detect perimeter in `NetClientBattle` loop (`abs(x)>=62.5 or abs(z)>=62.5`) and skip visual/root, then call `MapVisuals.build_outer_wall(_static_root)`. Host `Wall.gd` detects perimeter and skips `DecorMesh.wall_visual`; host BattleManager calls build outer wall after walls generation. But corners and base rings? Need design around existing outer perimeter gaps, base fountains, corners.

Alternative simpler: keep existing outer wall visuals but change them from boulder clusters to **flush-cut stone blocks** that tile; hide only gaps. Use 2m segments with 2.2m length; visually continuous. This works automatically in net client if `NetModels.wall` gets a style based on wall position and hq; but `NetModels.wall` lacks position; modify call to pass position or style. Could add `outer` flag in payload and `NetModels.wall(hq, outer)`; minimal changes in host Wall.gd and net. Build a **2m outer wall segment mesh** with stone courses and crenellations; 2m spacing with length2.05 gives continuous wall. Quality improved, seams minimal; but repeated segment pattern obvious, still "无缝结合" because flush. Corners/base rings still use old rocks; corner transitions could be rough.

Better continuous long wall: more impressive and truly seamless. Need scopes and time. Let's inspect map edge geometry: perimeter is not full square because corners at (-63,-63) and (63,63) are rounded; at (-62,62) base corner ring, (62,-62) base ring; lane edge walls cover segments. Could build outer wall along full **four sides** from corner to corner, with gaps at base fountains (radius5.3) perhaps. A continuous wall mesh can be built as a **ring path** with rounded corners / base cutouts, using segment meshes transformed along path. Easiest: generate one mesh with local segment length 2.0 for every perimeter step and add it to a single `MeshInstance3D`/MultiMesh; use `SurfaceTool` to append geometry at world positions, avoiding node seams. But still visual seams between 2m segment geometry if each segment has its own cap faces; can design **one continuous ribbon mesh** along a polyline with side faces, top, base—parametric; texture via vertex colors/UV? Procedural material uses world coordinate? `rock_material` shader uses `VERTEX`? Let's inspect rock_material shader.

1: extends RefCounted
2: ## 程序化墙体 / 草丛模型（替换 model/wall/wall.glb、model/grass/grass-large.glb）。
3: ## 全部为运行时生成的 ArrayMesh + 自定义 shader：无贴图、无外部资源；host 与 LAN 客户端共用，
4: ## 保证两端看到的是同一个模型。顶点数控制在千级以内（单次 draw call）。
5: 
6: static var _rock_mat: ShaderMaterial = null
7: static var _leaf_mat: ShaderMaterial = null
8: static var _rock_mesh: SphereMesh = null
9: static var _blob_mesh: SphereMesh = null
10: static var _blade_mesh: CylinderMesh = null
11: static var _wall_mesh_cache: ArrayMesh = null
12: static var _wall_variants: Array = []
13: static var _bush_variants: Array = []
14: 
15: # ==================== 材质 ====================
16: 
17: ## 石头材质：世界坐标噪声分色 + 顶部苔藓 + 底部泥土 + 细颗粒
18: static func rock_material() -> ShaderMaterial:
19: 	if _rock_mat != null:
20: 		return _rock_mat
21: 	var sh := Shader.new()
22: 	sh.code = _ROCK_CODE.replace("__NOISE__", _NOISE_GLSL)
23: 	_rock_mat = ShaderMaterial.new()
24: 	_rock_mat.shader = sh
25: 	return _rock_mat
26: 
27: ## 叶片材质：噪声深浅分色 + 顶部亮尖 + 随风摆动（GPU 顶点位移）
28: static func leaf_material() -> ShaderMaterial:
29: 	if _leaf_mat != null:
30: 		return _leaf_mat
31: 	var sh := Shader.new()
32: 	sh.code = _LEAF_CODE.replace("__NOISE__", _NOISE_GLSL)
33: 	_leaf_mat = ShaderMaterial.new()
34: 	_leaf_mat.shader = sh
35: 	return _leaf_mat
36: 
37: const _NOISE_GLSL := """
38: float hash13(vec3 p) {
39: 	p = fract(p * 0.3183099 + vec3(0.71, 0.113, 0.419));
40: 	p *= 17.0;
41: 	return fract(p.x * p.y * p.z * (p.x + p.y + p.z));
42: }
43: 
44: float vnoise(vec3 x) {
45: 	vec3 i = floor(x);
46: 	vec3 f = fract(x);
47: 	f = f * f * (3.0 - 2.0 * f);
48: 	float a = mix(hash13(i), hash13(i + vec3(1.0, 0.0, 0.0)), f.x);
49: 	float b = mix(hash13(i + vec3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0)), hash13(i + vec3(1.0, 1.0, 0.0)), f.x);
50: 	float c = mix(hash13(i + vec3(0.0, 0.0, 1.0)), hash13(i + vec3(1.0, 0.0, 1.0)), f.x);
51: 	float d = mix(hash13(i + vec3(0.0, 1.0, 1.0)), hash13(i + vec3(1.0, 1.0, 1.0)), f.x);
52: 	return mix(mix(a, b, f.y), mix(c, d, f.y), f.z);
53: }
54: """
55: 
56: const _ROCK_CODE := """
57: shader_type spatial;
58: render_mode diffuse_burley, specular_schlick_ggx;
59: 
60: uniform vec4 rock_a : source_color = vec4(0.47, 0.44, 0.39, 1.0);
61: uniform vec4 rock_b : source_color = vec4(0.21, 0.20, 0.18, 1.0);
62: uniform vec4 moss_col : source_color = vec4(0.19, 0.33, 0.12, 1.0);
63: uniform vec4 dirt_col : source_color = vec4(0.14, 0.12, 0.09, 1.0);
64: uniform float moss_band = 1.45;
65: 
66: varying vec3 wp;
67: varying vec3 wn;
68: 
69: __NOISE__
70: 
71: void vertex() {
72: 	wp = (MODEL_MATRIX * vec4(VERTEX, 1.0)).xyz;
73: 	wn = normalize((MODEL_MATRIX * vec4(NORMAL, 0.0)).xyz);
74: }
75: 
76: void fragment() {
77: 	float n = vnoise(wp * 2.4);
78: 	float n2 = vnoise(wp * 9.5);
79: 	float grains = vnoise(wp * 31.0);
80: 	vec3 base = mix(rock_b.rgb, rock_a.rgb, smoothstep(0.28, 0.78, n * 0.72 + n2 * 0.38));
81: 	base *= 0.82 + 0.38 * grains;
82: 	// 苔藓：靠近地面的朝上表面
83: 	float up = clamp(wn.y, 0.0, 1.0);
84: 	float moss = smoothstep(moss_band, 0.30, wp.y) * smoothstep(0.10, 0.72, up);
85: 	moss *= 0.55 + 0.80 * smoothstep(0.32, 0.78, vnoise(wp * 4.6 + vec3(7.0)));
86: 	base = mix(base, moss_col.rgb * (0.72 + 0.62 * n2), clamp(moss, 0.0, 1.0));
87: 	// 底部泥土
88: 	float dirt = smoothstep(0.45, 0.05, wp.y);
89: 	base = mix(base, dirt_col.rgb, dirt * 0.6);
90: 	ALBEDO = base;
91: 	ROUGHNESS = 0.95 - 0.12 * moss;
92: 	SPECULAR = 0.14;
93: }
94: """
95: 
96: const _LEAF_CODE := """
97: shader_type spatial;
98: render_mode diffuse_burley, specular_schlick_ggx, cull_back;
99: 
100: uniform vec4 leaf_dark : source_color = vec4(0.055, 0.16, 0.065, 1.0);
101: uniform vec4 leaf_mid : source_color = vec4(0.15, 0.33, 0.115, 1.0);
102: uniform vec4 leaf_lit : source_color = vec4(0.40, 0.60, 0.20, 1.0);
103: uniform float sway = 0.13;
104: uniform float sway_speed = 1.15;
105: 
106: varying vec3 wp;
107: varying float vh;
108: 
109: __NOISE__
110: 
111: void vertex() {
112: 	wp = (MODEL_MATRIX * vec4(VERTEX, 1.0)).xyz;
113: 	vh = clamp(VERTEX.y, 0.0, 3.0);
114: 	// 每个草丛按世界位置取相位，避免整片同步摆动
115: 	vec3 origin = (MODEL_MATRIX * vec4(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0)).xyz;
116: 	float ph = origin.x * 0.42 + origin.z * 0.33;
117: 	float t = TIME * sway_speed;
118: 	float gust = sin(t + ph) * 0.65 + sin(t * 1.63 + ph * 1.7) * 0.35;
119: 	float w = sway * vh * vh * 0.25;
120: 	VERTEX.x += gust * w;
121: 	VERTEX.z += gust * w * 0.55;
122: }
123: 
124: void fragment() {
125: 	float n = vnoise(wp * 4.2);
126: 	float n2 = vnoise(wp * 12.0 + vec3(4.0));
127: 	vec3 base = mix(leaf_dark.rgb, leaf_mid.rgb, smoothstep(0.22, 0.72, n));
128: 	base = mix(base, leaf_lit.rgb, smoothstep(0.45, 0.95, n2) * 0.78);
129: 	base = mix(base, leaf_lit.rgb, clamp(vh * 0.26, 0.0, 1.0) * 0.55);
130: 	ALBEDO = base;
131: 	ROUGHNESS = 0.72;
132: 	SPECULAR = 0.18;
133: 	BACKLIGHT = base * 0.55;
134: }
135: """

tools.name: ask_user_question

header.description: Optional short heading for the question, such as "Confirm" or "Choose Mode".

options.description: Optional choices to show the user. If you recommend one, put it first and append "(Recommended)" to that label.

description.description: One sentence explaining the tradeoff or impact.

multi_select.description: Whether the user may select more than one option. Defaults to false.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create a persisted goal that keeps this session working across automatic continuation rounds. Use it when the direct human request is a long-running objective, even if the user did not say "goal"; not for single-turn work.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend. Provide `file_path` before `old_string` and `new_string` in the arguments.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

tools.name: exit_plan_mode
tools.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: Read the current session goal, including the id and revision that update_goal requires.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files, not directories, whose paths match a glob pattern, including hidden and ignored files. Returns up to 100 paths in modification-time order; a larger result keeps the first paths and reports where the complete list was saved.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns up to 250 matches; a larger result reports where the complete match list was saved.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output

wait.description: Block until the job finishes or the timeout expires; a timed-out wait leaves the job running. Defaults to false.

tools.description: Get absolute paths to bundled Python and library directories, plus bundled Python distribution versions. Node.js and pnpm paths are included when the payload provides them. Python includes numpy, pandas, python-docx, python-pptx, openpyxl, Pillow, lxml, and XlsxWriter. Use these libraries for Office files unless the user or workspace instructions select another environment. When Node.js and pnpm paths are returned, run pnpm with that Node executable and pnpm script path. This does not change PATH or package-manager settings.

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "Get-Process" → "List running processes".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap; on expiry the command moves to the background as a job instead of being killed.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact command the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

Local times that do not exist in the zone are skipped; repeated local times fire once, at the earlier instant. After downtime, a recurring reminder delivers only its latest missed occurrence. Delivery can repeat after a crash.

title.description: Concise task name in the user's language, at most 120 characters. Name only the core action and subject; keep essential target identifiers such as PR numbers and branch names. Do not include execution frequency (e.g. daily, hourly), scheduled dates/times, time zones, task status, or configuration and execution details (e.g. read-only mode, profile-tag filters), even when embedded in the requested or existing title. tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a task list to plan multi-step work and show progress; skip it for trivial single-step tasks. Add one todo per concrete step before you start. While work remains, keep the todos being worked on `in_progress`, several only when work runs in parallel. Mark each todo `completed` as soon as it is done.

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the current goal.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

action.description: edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. complete and blocked are also allowed during an automatic continuation of this goal; blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Required only with action blocked: the concrete condition that persisted across rounds and blocks progress.

tools.name: wait_agent
tools.description: Wait for the next teammate status, message, or shared-task change after this call starts. This never wakes inactive members and returns noProgress immediately when no other member is running or provisioning. Re-list after wakeup or timeout instead of polling.

timeout_ms.description: Wait duration in milliseconds, from 10000 through 3600000. Defaults to 30000.

tools.name: web_fetch
tools.description: Fetch the content of a specific HTTP(S) URL and return it decoded to text.

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Search the web for current information. Returns an optional summary answer and a list of source URLs.

queries.description: 1–4 search queries; their results are merged.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

tools.name: working_directory
tools.description: Read the current working directory, or change it with cd. Relative paths use the current directory. Existing shells and running processes keep their own directories.

cd.description: Existing directory to enter. Omit to read the current directory.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend. Provide `file_path` before `content` in the arguments.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

Could camps near (±54,±54); arc walls max maybe58; classify outer if threshold54. That would be wrong (jungle camp walls become rampart). Need explicit marking.

Better explicit outer flag in Wall and network payload. It's only a few call sites:
- `_add_outer_wall` -> `_add_wall(..., outer=true)`.
- lane edge outermost 4 calls: `_add_wall(..., outer=true)`.
- base ring + seam filler? Those are part perimeter; mark outer=true too perhaps; but base ring curved 270° around fountain; using 2m straight segment model on 12° arc (chord.9) with length2.0 would overlap heavily; maybe keep rocks for base ring to form fountain; but transition. Could leave base ring old; outer straight edges stop at fountain; ring fills corner. "外周墙壁" sides should be seamless; base ring decorative.
- corner arcs: `_add_outer_wall` so outer=true; chord1.48, segment length2.0 overlap; could use **shorter segment mesh** for arc? Or use special curvature? At corner, 10 segments each chord1.48, 2m boxes overlap each other creating messy overlapping; maybe acceptable? Could use `DecorMesh.outer_wall_segment(length)` variant length based on wall? Hard.

Alternative explicit flag only for **straight perimeter edge walls** (lane outer + `_generate_outer_walls` edges). Corner arcs remain rocks. Then outer walls meet corner rocks at endpoints; gaps at corner? There are corner arc rocks at endpoint near edge; likely overlap. Better than overlap boxes.

But "地图外周墙壁" could include corner arcs but main sides matter.

Could instead **build a continuous outer rampart along entire fixed perimeter** in `MapVisuals` and hide all old visual for walls flagged outer, including corner? That's more work but best. Let's evaluate complexity:
- Add `MapVisuals.build_outer_wall(parent)` that creates one long mesh along a path polyline: four straight sides + rounded corners at (-63,-63),(63,63), plus cutouts around base fountains? Existing outer walls intentionally avoid fountain pools (distance5.3) so wall has gaps at base corners; base ring old rocks fills. A continuous wall would cut through fountain; could cut path around.
- Generate a **ring by emitting segments** along the perimeter path; each segment quad/box appended to one SurfaceTool mesh. Static mesh one draw call; world noise continuous; geometrybox segments flush. Since one mesh, no node seams. Could still use segment boxes but merged; seams only geometry if overlap; overlap fine.
- Call in host after map creation; hide old outer wall visuals. For network client, call same fixed method; skip old outer wall visuals. Need flag outer walls in payload or detect coordinate near edge; but client can simply skip all walls near perimeter (max>62.5 maybe) and build continuous; corner rocks remain? If build full perimeter including corners, skip old corner walls too? Could skip any wall within e.g. 9.0 of edge, but that includes base ring (would remove) and corner arcs; continuous perimeter could still have gaps at base corners if path excludes; base ring visuals needed. Hmm.

Maybe easiest: **replace per-wall outer straight segments with high-quality flush segments**, explicit flag. User sees seamless sides. Let's do that; minimal and network consistent. Need design model.

Implement `DecorMesh.outer_wall_visual(seed)` and `_build_outer_wall_mesh(rng)`:
- Box mesh.
- Local X tangent; total length L=2.08.
- Base plinth: `_append(box, (0,0.14,0), (2.08,0.28,1.18),0)` dark? material same.
- Main body 2.0 long, 0.9 thick, from 0.28 to2.35:
  - For course in 7: y=0.30+course*0.29; each course 3 blocks; widths .66; positions x=-.67,0,.67; thickness .92; height .27; slight jitter depth ±.02 and height; no horizontal gaps? Blocks at x edges -1.0,-.34,.34,1.0 flush; add 0.015 gap via width .65 leaving thin lines dark (material; but no dark mortar; gap empty reveals back? If blocks not touching, see through? They are solid boxes with depth .92; gap 0.015 shows interior/back face? Since no back wall, might see light through. Could add a **core back slab** behind blocks: box L2.0, height2.1, depth0.72 at z0; blocks on front/back? Simpler: use full body box, then add **protruding stone faces** on front and back as decorative blocks; no gaps.
  - Core body box (2.02,2.1,.86) at y1.33, z0. Color world noise; seams none.
  - Add **ashlar relief blocks** on both faces: for each course 7, 3 blocks, add thin boxes depth .08 at z=±.46, width .65, height .26, with small gaps; they protrude and create shadows/course lines. They also break silhouette? no.
  - Body ends flush at ±1.01.
  - Top cap continuous 2.06 x .18 x 1.12 at y2.47? body top2.38; cap center2.43 height.2.
  - Merlons: 3 blocks on top: width.48, depth1.0, height.38 at x -.68,0,.68, y2.73; gaps .2; appears crenellated. At segment ends blocks don't span to edge; adjacent segment repeats; gap at segment boundary .? last merlon center .68 width.48 ends .92, next segment starts -1.0 with merlon at -.68 width.48 starts-.92 => 0.16 gap centered at boundary (crenellation gap); natural.
  - Maybe vertical pilaster at center x0 width.18 depth1.02 from body y0.3 to2.5; every2m creates repeat; could look like columns, nice. But seam? center only; okay. Add on both faces? It's a box full depth, protrudes .04.
  - Base rubble: small rocks along base at local positions but must not extend beyond ±1.0; can add 3 rocks at x-.7,0,.7 z±.55, radius.12; continuous.
  - No moss disc (old had per-wall disc causing rings). Use material bottom dirt.
- Height3.1; collision 3.
- Seed variants 4 with minor jitter; shader noise world-based; blocks maybe same but jitter.

Need orientation: existing wall rotation local +Z = facing. Good. Segment length along X; use X.

Add static cache `_outer_variants`.

Modify `Wall.gd`:
```
var outer: bool = false
...
if outer:
 add_child(DecorMesh.outer_wall_visual(seed_v))
elif hq...
```
Set outer in `_add_wall` param default false; `_add_outer_wall` pass true; lane edge outer calls pass true; seam filler around base maybe? Leave false to keep rocks. Corner arcs via `_add_outer_wall` pass true; segment length2.0 on chord1.48 overlaps (two segments overlap by0.52; boxes intersect but flush-ish, may look bulky/double detail). Could instead create `outer_wall_visual` with segment length dynamic? Add optional length parameter and build cache per bucket? Simpler: corner arcs use old rocks by changing `_add_outer_wall`? `_add_outer_wall` called both edges and corners. Add param `outer_style=true`; corner call `_add_outer_wall(..., false)`? Then junction; maybe okay.
Better use a smaller outer model for corner? Could build `outer_wall_visual(seed, span)` where span length =1.55 for corners, cache by span. But `Wall` only knows position, not span. We could set `wall.outer_len`; `_add_outer_wall` for corner passes len1.55; for edges 2.08. Then mesh variants cache keyed length. This makes corners continuous and high quality. More code but manageable:
- `Wall.gd var outer_len: float = 2.08`, `outer: bool`.
- `_add_wall(pos,facing,force,hq,outer=false,outer_len=2.08)` set.
- `_add_outer_wall(pos,facing,force? no)` needs know corner? Current called for edges and arcs. Add param `length := 2.08`; edge calls default; corner arc call with 1.55. But `_add_outer_wall` also skips base fountains. Signature `func _add_outer_wall(pos, facing, len := 2.08)`. Corner calls `_add_outer_wall(..., 1.55)`. `_add_wall(..., true, false, true, len)`.
- Lane edge outer calls pass outer true default2.08.
- Base seam filler walls at exact edges (x=-63,z57.5 etc) need outer true; they are along edge, length2.08 but they fill gap between ring and straight wall; could mark outer. The normal wall orientation facing inward; good.
- Base ring itself remains old rocks; transition at seam filler.

But if length parameter varies, `DecorMesh.outer_wall_visual(seed, length)` builds variants per length bucket; corners use1.55. Add cache dictionary keyed `int(round(length*100))` or simply build each 4 variants for requested length; only 1.55 and2.08 so 8 variants.

Need ensure collision boxes still step2; outer visual length2.08 overlaps .08; corners1.55 vs chord1.48 overlap .07. Excellent seamless.

Network payload: add `outer` bool and `outer_len` maybe. But client can infer from coordinates? To match corners, need flags. Add 5th/6th entries:
`walls.append([x,z,rot,is_hq,1 if outer else0, outer_len])`
NetClientBattle parse:
```
var outer= w.size()>4 and int(w[4])==1
var olen=float(w[5]) if w.size()>5 else 2.08
var wall_model=NetModels.wall(hq,outer,olen)
```
NetModels.wall signature; calls elsewhere? Search.

  （脚本已就绪，失败会静默降级，不阻断交付）。

## Project Overview

HonorKing — a 3D MOBA game built with **Godot 4.5** (Forward Plus renderer). All game logic is written in **GDScript**. The game simulates a 5v5 Honor of Kings-style match: one player-controlled hero plus 4 AI teammates versus 5 AI enemies across a three-lane map with jungle, turrets, and epic monsters.

## Development Commands

- **Run the game**: Open `project.godot` in the Godot 4.5 editor and press F5, or run `godot --path .` from the project root.
- **No tests, no build step**: There is no test suite or CI. The only way to verify changes is to run the game in the Godot editor.

## Architecture

### Autoloads (Globals)

Defined in `project.godot` → `[autoload]`. These singletons are available everywhere without `load()`:

| Autoload | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `Config` | `scripts/core/Config.gd` | Constants: `MAP_SIZE=120`, `Team` enum (`PLAYER=0, ENEMY=1, NEUTRAL=2`) |
| `ItemDatabase` | `assets/ItemDatabase.gd` | All item definitions, synthesis trees, recommended build paths, `get_item()`, `can_build()`, `get_synthesis_cost()` |
| `SkillDatabase` | `assets/SkillDataBase.gd` | All skill definitions (hero skills + summoner spells), `get_skill()` |
| `GameManager` | `scripts/core/GameManager.gd` | Stub — currently empty (`_ready` and `_process` are no-ops) |
| `UiManager` | `scripts/ui/UI_Manager.gd` | Comprehensive UI: skill icons, shop, kill feed, hero detail panel (C key), target info, death recap, buff panel, damage/gold/heal popups |
| `CollisionSystem` | `scripts/core/CollisionSystem.gd` | Per-frame entity pushback to prevent overlapping (heroes ← → turrets, minions ← → turrets excluded) |

### Core Scripts (`scripts/core/`)

- **`BattleManager.gd`** — The central game controller (`class_name BattleManager`). Handles:
  - Map creation (ground planes, lane planes, river, high-ground circles)
  - Hero select UI → game start flow
  - Player hero + AI hero creation (one of each role: assassin/mage/marksman/warrior/support)
  - Turret, jungle camp, wall/bush placement
  - Minion wave spawning (3 lanes × 2 teams, with growth tables, siege/super/dragon minion variants)
  - Epic monster timers (Tyrant at 4min, Dragon at 4min)
  - Economy systems: kill/assist gold, tower gold, lane gold sharing, natural gold/exp, jungle item rules, support item rules
  - Input handling: left-click attack order, right-click move, raycasting for ground/target selection
  - Camera: follows player hero, minimap drag/jump override
  - Win condition: crystal destruction → game-over screen
  - Hero configs: `hero_configs` dictionary with base stats for all 17 heroes

- **`EntityDatabase.gd`** — Stub (empty `_ready`/`_process`).

- **`CameraController.gd`** — Standalone camera script (attached to a Camera3D), follows a `@export var target`. Currently unused — BattleManager controls the camera directly.

- **`MapGenerator.gd`** — Alternative map generator (creates a simpler 60×60 grass + river). Not used in the main game; BattleManager has its own `_create_map()`.

- **`CollisionSystem.gd`** — See Autoloads above.

### Entity Hierarchy (`scripts/entities/`)

All entities inherit from **`GameEntity`** (`class_name GameEntity extends CharacterBody3D`):

```
GameEntity
├── Hero (player & AI champions)
├── Turret (defensive structures)
├── Minion (lane creeps)
├── JungleMonster (neutral camps + epic monsters)
├── Bullet (projectile for ranged attacks and skill shots)
├── LinearBullet (directional projectile variant)
├── Wall (terrain obstacle)
├── Bush (stealth zone)
├── HealthPack (regen pickup)
├── TeleportZone (teleport pad)
└── prw (unidentified entity)
```

**`GameEntity`** provides:
- Base stats: `health`, `max_health`, `attack`, `armor`, `magic_resist`, `move_speed`, `attack_range`, `attack_speed`, `body_radius`, `level`
- State effects: slow, stun, knockup, freeze, suppress, silence, grievous wounds
- Shield system (`shield_remaining`/`shield_timer`)
- Marker system for stacking passives (e.g., Zhen Ji freeze, Angela burn, Marco Polo stacks)
- Damage calculation: `take_damage()` with armor/MR reduction formula (`resistance / (resistance + 602)`), penetration, crit detection
- Hunt DoT system (jungle item burn)
- Lifesteal application (physical and magical, with grievous wounds reduction)
- Death handling: `die(killer)` → signals, gold/exp distribution, buff transfer
- Kill assist detection (nearest enemy hero within 12 units)

**`Hero`** (`scripts/entities/Hero.gd`, ~2150 lines) — The largest and most complex class:
- **Stats**: base stats + role-based growth per level (tank/warrior/assassin/marksman/mage/support)
- **Equipment**: 6-slot inventory, `buy_equipment()` with component synthesis, `_apply_equipment_bonuses()` recalculates all stats from items, 100+ unique item passive/active effects
- **Skills**: 3 hero skills + summoner spell + recover, each with cooldowns, mana costs, charge/restore system, upgrade via Ctrl+key or auto-level
- **Hero-specific logic**: Each hero has hardcoded special behavior in `_physics_process()` (Arthur passive heal + W shield rotation, Donghuang orbs, Li Bai sword auras, Zhang Fei transformation + mana, Lanling stealth, Taiyi Q channeling)
- **Combat**: auto-attack with bullet spawning (ranged) or instant (melee), crit, on-hit effects from 20+ items
- **Input**: WASD movement, right-click move orders, left-click attack orders, skill hotkeys 1-3, summoner spell key, item actives (keys 6-0, V, =, -)
- **Post-game stats**: `damage_dealt_to_heroes`, `damage_taken_from_heroes`, `healing_done`, `cc_duration_dealt`, `turret_damage`, `jungle_gold`, `last_hits`, `gold_history`

**Other entity notes**:
- `Bullet.gd` / `LinearBullet.gd` — Projectiles with speed, damage, pierce, slow, red buff burn, team affiliation
- `Turret.gd` — Auto-attacks nearby enemies, has outer/inner/high/crystal tiers with different stats
- `Minion.gd` — Follows waypoints along lanes, attacks enemies in range
- `JungleMonster.gd` — Has `activity_radius` (leash range), `buff_type` for red/blue buff
- `Wall.gd` / `Bush.gd` — Static collision/stealth volumes
- `HeroAI.gd` — AI controller for bot heroes (attached as child of Hero)

### Asset Scripts (`assets/`)

- **`ItemDatabase.gd`** — Massive dictionary of all equipment items with: name, tier (1-4), cost, stat bonuses, `requires` (synthesis components), `passive`/`active` descriptions, category tags. Key functions: `get_item(id)`, `can_build(id, owned)`, `get_synthesis_cost()`, `get_synthesis_tree()`, `get_recommended_items(role)`.
- **`SkillDataBase.gd`** — Dictionary of all skills (hero abilities + summoner spells). Each skill defines: `type` (0=targeted, 1=AoE, 3=linear, 4=dash, 6=shield), `cooldown`, `mana_cost`, `cast_range`, `damage`, `radius`, `duration`, etc.
- **`Skill.gd`** — Skill resource class (`class_name Skill extends Resource`). Properties: `skill_name`, `type`, `cooldown`, `cd_bonus`, `mana_cost`, `power_bonus`, `cast_range`, `cast_time`, `damage`, `radius`, `duration`, `self_displacement`, `shield_amount`, `is_channeling`, `charge`, `restore`, `restore_bonus`.

### UI System (`scripts/ui/`)

**`UI_Manager.gd`** (~1600 lines) handles all in-game UI:
- Skill bar with 8 icon slots (4 skills + summoner + 2 active equipment)
- Shop system (O key): categorized grid (物理/法术/防御/靴子/打野/游走/保命), detail panel, buy/sell, component synthesis display
- Recommended equipment (B key to quick-buy)
- Kill feed (multi-kill announcements, tower/epic monster kills)
- Hero detail panel (C key): team stats, all hero cards with stats/skills/equipment/KDA
- Death recap (auto-shows on death): damage source breakdown with stacked bar charts
- Target detail panel (shows selected target's stats)
- Buff/debuff display panel
- Damage/heal/gold floating numbers (world-space → screen projection)
- Respawn widgets (hero icons with HP rings and respawn timers)

Internal classes: `SkillIcon` (draws cooldown overlay, upgrade indicator), `RespawnWidget` (HP ring + death timer), `DamageChart`.

### Key Mechanics to Understand

1. **Damage formula**: `actual_damage = raw_damage × (1 - resistance / (resistance + 602))` where resistance already accounts for flat and percentage penetration.
2. **Attack speed**: Uses a threshold table (Model A from Honor of Kings) — panel AS% maps to discrete attack interval tiers.
3. **Economy sharing**: Multiple heroes near a minion kill split gold (100%/80%/55%/43%/37% for 1-5 players). Jungle/support items modify this.
4. **Minion growth**: Minion stats interpolate from growth tables at `game_time / 60` minutes, with melee/ranged/siege/super/dragon variants.
5. **Item synthesis**: Buying a high-tier item that requires owned components only costs the difference. Selling refunds 70%.
6. **Buff system**: Active buffs are stored as dictionaries with timers, processed each frame in `_calculate_buff()`. Red/blue buffs transfer on kill.
7. **Hero-specific code**: Each hero has unique mechanics hardcoded with `if display_name == "..."` checks in `_physics_process()`, `_perform_attack()`, and `_finish_casting()`. Adding a new hero requires touching Hero.gd in multiple places plus adding skill definitions to SkillDatabase.

### Assets Not Tracked in Scripts

- `icon.svg` — Game icon
- `.godot/` — Engine cache (shader cache, editor state, import files)
- `scenes/battle.tscn` — The single main scene (binary .tscn format)
- 3D models, textures, and audio are created programmatically (PlaneMesh, CapsuleMesh, TorusMesh, StandardMaterial3D) — there are no imported art assets.

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "Get-Process" → "List running processes".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap; on expiry the command moves to the background as a job instead of being killed.
